readBy: the builder of Round 1310, desktop Claude lane (session H's workflow)
method: Each page was opened on the read day through a page reader that answers with lines quoted from the page; no figure comes from a search summary. Every literal is a line that reader quoted; a table row is written as its cells in order with single spaces between them (runs of spaces in a fixed width table collapsed to one). A page's en dash or em dash is written as a hyphen, since the repo bans both. A figure is the number printed in its literal. USED, THIN and DISPUTED are not written in the data: scripts/simCmLeagueBookFacts.mjs works them out from the rows on every run.
limits: No copy of a page was kept, so there is no snapshot hash. A reader who doubts a figure opens the url and finds the literal.
The page reader quotes at most about 125 characters a line, so a long sentence is quoted in part; the part kept holds the figure.
myKhel's Premier League list carries no date; the league's own list (premierleague.com/en/news/1206108) is dated 19 May 2024 and has since been brought up to 2024/25. Both were read on 2026-10-12.

The matches a club played come from format rows only: for the Premier League the league's own guide (20 clubs since 1995/96, 38 matches a club) and RSSSF's final table of each season, whose last line is position 20 with 38 played. 2019-20 stands on two final tables of that season (RSSSF and ESPN), each with 38 played.

The Bundesliga: the league's own history of its top scorers (bundesliga.com news 19353, dated 27.05.2025) and RSSSF's list of German top scorers agree on all ten seasons. Its matches come from the league's own FAQ (18 teams since 1965/66 but for 1991/92; the page prints no day, only that the league enters its 64th season in 2026/27, so its published field is the year) and RSSSF's final table of each season, and 2019-20 from RSSSF and ESPN, each with 34 played.

RSSSF serves its pages in a Latin-1 encoding and the page reader showed each umlaut as a replacement mark (M?nchen); the literals here restore the letter (München, Köln, Nürnberg, Fürth, Füllkrug, Suárez, Mbappé, Málaga, Atlético, Alavés). Nothing else in a literal was changed. The league's line for 2022/23 ends in a stray hyphen on the page and keeps it.

La Liga: no page of LaLiga's own listing its top scorers by season was found (two searches of laliga.com on 2026-10-12; its matchday 38 results pages print no table), so neither publisher is the league. RSSSF's Pichichi list is Marca's count by the page's own words; 90min's list (2023-05-26, ends at 2021/22) and ESPN's own scoring table of each season are the second publisher. 2021-22 is DISPUTED: RSSSF prints 37 for Benzema where 90min and ESPN print 27, and it stays on file unused. The matches come from RSSSF's and ESPN's final tables of each season, each with 38 played (ESPN's page splits a row into cells and the reader listed them by column; they are written in the page's column order, GP first).

Serie A: no page of the league's own listing its top scorers was opened (the search gave none). RSSSF's list of Serie A top scorers gives all ten; Sky Sport Italia's list (2020-09-14, to 2019/20, one card a season: the reader gave each card's season and name and quoted its count line) and 90min's list (2023-06-02, to 2021/22; its 2022/23 line reads TBC and is no reading) agree with it, and ESPN's own scoring table of 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25 is the second publisher there. Every reading on file agrees. The matches come from RSSSF's and ESPN's final tables of each season, each with 38 played.
